Ḍhuṇḍhirāja

V. p. 268a) an. younger brother of Nāganātha; belonged to the latter half of 15th Cent. Ref. to in Bhaviṣyapurāṇa, III. 4. 13.
--Jātakābharaṇa. jy. IO. 3075-8. MT. 1933.
See Dikshit, Bhāratīya Jyotiṣa (Hindi edn.). p.. 370-71. 376-7.

Ḍhuṇḍhirāja(vyāsayajvan)
resident of Svāmimalai; son of Lakṣmaṇa Vyāsa; patronized by Tryambakarāya Makhin (a. of Dharmākūta), Kings Śāhaji an. Serfoji of Tanjore, an. Raghunātha (son of Nārāyaṇādhvarin an. minister of the Tanjore King Śivāji); describes himself a. the Paurāṇika of King Śāhaji an. a. Abhinavajayadeva, TD. 10957; visited Benares an. sent to Tanjore a rare ms. of Jagannātha's Jñānavilāsakāvya, TD. 3792.
--Dharmākūta, a. exposition of the Rāmāyaṇa from D.. Śāstra standpoint; [Page012-a. ascribed to his patron Tryambakarāya; written in 1719 A. D. TD. 9385.
--C. on Mudrārākṣasa, composed in 1714 A. D. a. the instance of Tryambakarāya.
Pt.. Bomb. Skt. Ser. 27. Bombay, 1900.
--Rājakośanighaṇṭu. lex. ascribed to his patron Raghunātha. TD. 5029.
--Śāhavilāsagīta on Śāhajī. TD. 10957-8.
See V. Raghavan, Intro. to Śāhendravilāsa, p.. 26-7. 55.
